task_context.title: Consolidate cas-cli's 107 integration test binaries into a few test harnesses to cut test build and link time
task_context.description: Measured 2026-09-29: cas-cli/tests has 107 top-level *.rs files (plus 13 support dirs). task_context.acceptance_criteria: Integration test executables drop from 107 to at most 10; the full suite passes with the same test count; release-gate and CI references are updated; measured build-time improvement is recorded in the task.

criteria: At most ten integration harnesses preserve every previously executed integration test.

task_context.title: Close gates dead-end after a supervisor git merge: proof_scope_fix says "requires a merged delivery transaction", legacy per-file --test proof demanded after test consolidation, content-drop anchor pinned across request_changes
task_context.description:
This happened on 2026-09-29 during 3.38.0. The supervisor merged worker branches into the epic with plain `git merge` plus a push; it did not use factory worktree_merge. Four tasks then could not close through any path the gates themselves suggest.
(1) cas-4245 and cas-d0fb: the close gate says "widen with task update proof_targets=… proof_scope_fix=true". A supervisor update with a strictly wider list after the merge still fails with "PROOF-SCOPE FIX REJECTED: parse error: proof correction requires a merged or close-ready delivery transaction or an authenticated merge observation on the task's WorkTarget". The worktree is an ancestor of the epic tip, and "parse error" is a misleading prefix.
(2) cas-d0fb: a supervisor_override close is rejected by the scoped-proof gate. It demands `SCOPED_PROOF_BASE=… scripts/run-scoped-tests.sh --proof -p cas --test retrieval_eval_test --test distributed_factory_test …`, but those --test targets no longer exist after cas-d0fb consolidated them into 10 harnesses. Workers also can't run it (cas-4cbb), and the gate ignores that the epic's ASSEMBLY_PROOF is the policy.
(3) cas-4b3a: DELIVERY CONTENT DROPPED stays pinned to the original anchor 889c7f1d after request_changes and a re-delivery at tip cdf539e0 (identical to the epic). No override path exists.
Workers end up blocked, and their status=blocked updates are refused by DELIVERY PROOF SCOPE LOCKED.
task_context.acceptance_criteria: An ancestor-of-target check (the delivery tip reachable from the target tip) counts as a merge observation for proof_scope_fix, and the message drops "parse error". The scoped-proof close gate accepts an epic ASSEMBLY_PROOF note in place of a worker scoped receipt, per the cas-4cbb policy, and maps legacy test stems through scripts/cas-test-targets.py. The content-drop check measures the current delivery anchor after request_changes. The supervisor-override close honors an explicit reviewed-drop reason. Workers may set status=blocked while proof-scope locked. Regressions cover each case.

cases.defect: Recovery fixture supplies caller updated_at as the optimistic-lock token, although TaskStore::update owns and returns the stored timestamp.
cases.expected_fix: Use update return token; retain a stale-token rejection and unchanged Blocked status assertion.
criteria: Proof-scope recovery works after a blocker report.
A stale optimistic-lock token must still refuse recovery.

task_context.title: Supervisor relays silently abandoned: the Claude team tree (config.json + inboxes/) vanishes mid-session and the daemon retries ENOENT 15× then drops the message
task_context.description:
ROOT CAUSE (verified 2026-09-29, session cas-src-cosmic-crow-66): the daemon delivers to the Claude supervisor through Claude Code native Agent Teams inbox files at $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/teams/<session>/inboxes/<name>.json (TeamsManager, cas-cli/src/ui/factory/daemon/runtime/teams.rs; CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/home/pippenz/.claude-pippenz@gmail.com). Partway through the session, teams/cas-src-cosmic-crow-66/config.json and inboxes/ disappeared; only three worker *-settings.json files remain.

From 2026-09-29T16:17:10Z on, every supervisor-bound delivery failed "No such file or directory (os error 2)". After 15 attempts over ~900s it is marked last_pending_reason=abandoned_unknown_target (crates/cas-store/src/prompt_queue_store.rs ~5352-5422). 48 rows, 16:17:10Z to 19:08:37Z, e.g. prompt_queue ids 1738360 and 1738462. No alert, no fallback. Messages were seen only when the supervisor was already mid-turn and the turn-start hook surfaced pending rows (e.g. id 1734907), which is why it looked intermittent and why finished deliveries waited 25–60 min.

Very likely the same cause as cas-5129 (Claude worker spawns never start): Claude workers join via --team-name and need the team's config.json. The last good Claude spawn was 15:57Z; later ones hung with no transcript. Codex workers are unaffected. Still unknown: what deleted config.json and inboxes/ between 15:57Z and 16:17Z. Candidates: Claude Code team cleanup (a teammate exit, TeamDelete, a Claude CLI update/restart), cas update's `.claude` sync, or a Cassy reaper. Find it from logs or reproduce.

Fix:
(1) Before each inbox write, verify the team tree and recreate config.json and inboxes/ idempotently from the daemon's own spawn record if missing, logging loudly.
(2) Never retry ENOENT 15× in silence: on the first failure, fall back to PTY prompt injection for the supervisor, and surface a Commander/operator alert naming the missing path.
(3) Treat an abandoned merge-ready relay as an incident (worker_status red and an operator ping).
(4) Find and stop whatever deletes the tree.
Regression test: delete the team tree mid-session and assert the next supervisor relay is still delivered within 60s.
task_context.acceptance_criteria: A test where a worker parks for merge while the supervisor is idle shows the supervisor woken within 60s; worker_status shows zero undelivered merge-ready relays older than 60s in a live session; the root cause is named with evidence.

cases.defect: Abandoned relay fixture unwraps a transition to Delivered, although both are rank-3 terminal siblings and the transition is rejected.
cases.expected_fix: Assert rejection, unchanged Abandoned stage, absent delivery timestamp and continued forensic reporting.
criteria: An abandoned unknown-target relay remains reportable.
Terminal sibling states cannot be rewritten as successful delivery.
